summary: The Orthodox Confession of Peter Mogila, a seventeenth-century confession of the Orthodox churches, teaches that baptism is the first of seven mysteries (sacraments): a washing away of original sin by being immersed three times in water in the name of the Trinity, after which a person, born again of water and the Spirit, is restored to God's grace. It is given once and is not repeated. Infants are baptized, with a sponsor who renounces the devil and confesses the creed on their behalf; adults do this themselves. The confession calls baptism an undoubted seal and pledge of eternal salvation. The questions read do not say whether baptism is necessary for salvation.

points.question: What is baptism?
points.answer: The first mystery: a washing away and rooting out of original sin by three immersions in water with the Trinitarian formula, after which a person is born again of water and the Spirit and restored to God's grace, with the way opened into the Kingdom of Heaven.

points.question: Who receives it, and what is asked of them?
points.answer: Infants, whose sponsor renounces the devil and confesses the creed for them, and adults, who make these renunciations and the confession of faith themselves.

points.question: How is it given?
points.answer: By dipping the person three times in pure, natural water while the minister says the Trinitarian formula. It is ordinarily given by a minister; in urgent necessity any person, man or woman, may baptize with water and the same words.

points.question: What does it give?
points.answer: It is called an undoubted seal and pledge of eternal salvation, with fruits and benefits the confession goes on to list.

points.question: Can it be repeated?
points.answer: No, provided the person who baptized believed rightly in the Trinity and used the right words.

excerpt.text: But this Mystery being once received, is not to be again repeated.

scriptureNote: The only passage cited in the questions read.

review.note: Questions 101-103 read on 2026-11-12 in the azbyka.ru English text; the rest of Question 103 (the fruits of baptism) was not read. The date and the patriarchs' endorsement come from general knowledge. The Confession of Dositheus (1672), which also covers baptism, was not retrievable in full and has not been used.
